newsitem.title: CHINA: China's disasters kill 68, cost $208 million.
newsitem.headline: China's disasters kill 68, cost $208 million.

text.p: Natural disasters in China caused 68 deaths and property damage totalling 1.73 billion yuan ($208.4 million) in the first three months of the year, the China Insurance Daily said on Tuesday.
Earthquakes in the far northwestern region of Xinjiang and in southwestern Yunnan province, killed 12 people, seriously injured 44 and affected 250,000, the newspaper said.
More than 200,000 buildings had been destroyed, resulting in direct losses of 563 million yuan, it said.
Drought across northern China affected nearly 5.5 million people, 6.2 million hectares (15.3 million acres) of winter wheat and more than 4.4 million heads of livestock, it said.

Frigid temperatures late last year and in January this year in Xinjiang and the northeastern province of Liaoning killed at least 98,000 heads of livestock and caused direct economic losses of 1.03 billion yuan.
Hailstorms killed two people, injured 152, harmed 21,370 hectares (52,800 acres) of crops and damaged more than 270,000 buildings, creating direct losses of more than 78 million yuan.
One hailstorm that struck Chongqing in southwestern Sichuan province in early March rained lumps of ice up to 3.5 cm (1.4 in), causing 45 million yuan in damages, it said.
Natural disasters affected more than 300 million people in China last year and relief for disaster victims totalled a record 6.0 billion yuan, official figures show.
State media has said that floods in 1996 caused losses of more than 200 billion yuan.
The People's Insurance Group, China's largest insurer, was expected to pay out a total of 3.7 billion yuan in compensation for flood-related damage last year.
